answer: Time-locked contribution chains. Each identity must perform verifiable useful work (e.g., labeled data or compute) and sell it to a buyer whose rating depends on a rolling horizon of past transactions. New identities start at a reputation nadir and can only climb through sustained sales, with ranking weight rising as a lotus-like tiered layer per verified delivery. Sybils must fund parallel work pipelines and wait through the full horizon before their identities gain influence; each fake account costs real labor plus idle time, not just money.
